lesson.title: Non-consensual intimate synthetic media
lesson.summary: Assess identifiable intimate synthetic material, exact consent and the limited manipulation boundary without graphic examples.

prerequisites.reason: The consent condition is examined within the elements of the added prohibition.

blocks: The new **intimate-media provision** concerns AI generating/manipulating realistic intimate or sexually explicit material of an identifiable natural person without that person's freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation/manipulation.
This lesson uses legal descriptions only. It needs no real material, demonstrations or identifiable person's images. Each stated subject, realism, identification and consent element must be checked.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(ba), 5(1b), 5(1a); Article 113(a)

blocks: An **intimate-media consent test** concerns consent for the particular generation or manipulation, not merely a prior agreement to take an ordinary photograph. Silence, an unrelated form or public availability does not establish the specified consent.
Fictional Northbridge safeguarding case: ordinary-image permission exists but no consent for intimate synthesis. The prior permission does not by itself establish the new provision's consent element.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(ba), 5(1b), 5(1a); Article 113(a)

blocks: Article 5(1b) gives a limited **manipulation boundary**: altering material without increasing exposure of depicted intimate parts or changing the nature of depicted sexually explicit activities does not constitute manipulation for point (ba).
Do not turn this exact boundary into a general exemption for all editing. Record what actually changes. The separate generation branch and other legal rules still need examination.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(ba), 5(1b), 5(1a); Article 113(a)

blocks: These new provisions apply from **2 December 2026** in the working baseline. Paragraph 1a further distinguishes supply and use, taught next in B12. The present lesson establishes content/consent and manipulation elements.
A full conclusion must apply that actor-specific qualification and date. Other laws may already forbid conduct; this future application date is not permission to exploit people before it.

questions.prompt: A person permitted an ordinary photograph, but did not consent to intimate synthetic generation. What follows for this element?

options.blocks: The specified generation consent is not established
options.reason: Consent must concern the particular generation/manipulation with the stated qualities.

options.blocks: All later synthetic uses are automatically permitted
options.reason: Unrelated prior permission is not the specified consent.

options.blocks: Public availability supplies every consent quality
options.reason: Availability does not establish freely given specific explicit consent.
